assertions.title: Batch resize failure downgrades to frame presentation in the same host session

assertions.title: Batch render failure downgrades to frame presentation and still presents the triggering frame

evidence.notes: The tests verify 2x device-pixel coordinates convert 200x100 to logical 100x50 and 100x200 to 50x100 / 300x400 to 150x200, while pointer leave routes through the host to a pointerExitedWindow event.

assertions.title: Wheel and horizontal-scroll events convert correctly across host and runtime

evidence.notes: The suite verifies 2x scaled wheel input maps 200x100 to 100x50 with delta 3.0 preserved, and horizontal scroll maps 400x300 to 200x150 with delta -5.0 and axis .horizontal preserved.

assertions.title: Host refresh-rate updates control runtime pacing and timer behavior

steps.action: Run the focused WinSwiftUIWindowHostTests suite and inspect timer and refresh-rate tests
steps.expected: Refresh-rate, idle suppression, and active-input pacing tests all pass.

evidence.notes: The tests verify refresh-rate changes from 60Hz to 144Hz update timer cadence and runtime minimumFrameInterval, idle animation frames disable the timer, and a resize plus sustained pointer input keeps timer pumping enabled while presentation remains dirty.

assertions.title: Observed-object reloads coalesce by turn and dependency relevance

steps.action: Run the focused WinSwiftUIWindowHostTests suite and inspect observed-object reload tests
steps.expected: Same-turn relevant changes coalesce to one rebuild, and irrelevant dependency changes do not trigger redundant rebuilds.

evidence.notes: The suite proves three same-turn relevant object changes schedule exactly one deferred reload and one follow-up render, while an irrelevant observed object change finishes a deferred task with didReload == false and queues no render; companion tests verify pending changed object accumulation and unique registration tracking.
